## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`save_report` must stop reporting success when the write fails. Right now it swallows `OSError`, prints "Report saved to …" and returns 0, so users are told a report exists when it does not.

## Changes
The pull request adds `save_report`, which writes the rendered report and announces where it went, and `cleanup_report`, which removes an optional temporary report and ignores a missing file. It also adds pytest cases for both.

## Critical
- app/reports.py:8 — silent-failure — Propagate write errors from save_report — When `path` is in a missing directory or is read-only, `except OSError: pass` discards the error. Execution then continues to `print(f"Report saved to {path}")` and `return 0`. The caller cannot tell that the save failed. — Users and scripts get a success message and exit code 0 for a report that was never written. — Fix: Remove the `try`/`except` or re-raise the error, or print an actionable error and return a non-zero status instead of falling through to the success message.

## Important
- tests/test_reports.py:13 — tests — Assert the failure outcome for an unavailable destination — `test_save_with_unavailable_destination` calls `save_report(tmp_path / "missing" / "report.txt")` and asserts nothing about the return value, output or exception. It passes whether the failure is reported or swallowed. — The failed-save path has no regression protection, so the false-success defect above passes this test. — Fix: Assert `pytest.raises(OSError)` or a non-zero return with no "Report saved" output, depending on which error contract the fix chooses.
